adds.rationale: Russia's February 24, 2022 invasion of Ukraine triggered a buildup-phase rotation into US defense primes on expectations of a protracted conflict and rising NATO defense budgets; Lockheed Martin is the most directly and repeatedly cited beneficiary, and the watchlist currently has zero exposure to the profile's named 'geopolitical realignment: defense & rearmament' wave.

removes.rationale: With the watchlist pinned at the 5-ticker cap, SPY's broad cap-weighted structure gives only trace exposure to the aerospace & defense rotation now underway and duplicates beta already embedded in the four mega-cap holdings; freeing the slot for LMT lets the watchlist capture the newly-active geopolitical wave the profile names, which a passive S&P tracker cannot represent at this size.

news_evidence.summary: War stocks (Lockheed Martin, Northrop) surging roughly 20% since the invasion, a sector rotation a broad S&P 500 tracker only thinly captures

rationale_overall: Net effect: the watchlist trades its undifferentiated S&P 500 slot for a direct stake in the geopolitical realignment/defense-rearmament wave that Russia's February 24 invasion of Ukraine just put into a clear buildup phase, while the four AI-adjacent mega-caps (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, NVDA) are kept unchanged — AAPL's Q1 FY22 print (record $123.9B revenue, +11% YoY, beat estimates in every category but iPads) shows no thesis breach, and nothing dated within the lookback window suggests the AI wave has crested. Quantum computing (Rigetti, listed 2022-03-02) and rockets/robotics/nuclear candidates were surveyed but rejected this quarter: Rigetti has under a month of trading history and no liquidity track record, and no dated, in-window news bullet could be found tying a rockets/robotics/nuclear ticker to a concrete milestone, so those waves are deferred rather than forced. The SPY removal is a capacity judgment call rather than a classic thesis-breach or peak-enthusiasm case — flagged here for transparency.
